Welcome from the Headteacher
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Cyril Jackson - an ambitious, successful and inclusive community school.
The expectations for our pupils and ourselves know no bounds and we strive for excellence in all that we do.
We lay the foundations for every child to succeed. Cyril Jackson offers a curriculum which engages and inspires, a diverse range of educational visits and experiences, outstanding pastoral care and high expectations, all delivered within a happy, safe and supportive environment.
Hodo Dirir Headteacher

Behaviours & Attitudes
To ensure all pupils are reflective, analytical and active independent learners.
Personal Development
To ensure that children are fully active citizens within the school community.
Quality Of Education
To ensure all pupils achieve highly in order to fulfil interests, aspirations for the future and meet their creative potential.
Leadership & Management
To ensure that teachers’ subject knowledge and pedagogy builds over time translating into improvements in the teaching of the curriculum.
Early Years
To ensure that children acquire a wide vocabulary, communicate effectively and acquire a knowledge of phonics giving them the foundations for future learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast Club - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
The Breakfast Club at Cyril Jackson School is available every day from 8am in the North Building Hall; however there is a limited number of places available and parents will be required to apply if they wish their child to attend on a full or part-time basis. Letters will be distributed periodically over the course of the academic year to ensure the club runs at full capacity. Priority places will be given to working parents.
A small charge is payable per day: £3 for working parents; 50p non-working parents.
A member of staff will escort children from Year 5 and 6 to their designated playground and those children from Nursery to Year 4 will be escorted to their designated teacher or member of support staff.
Fees will be added to your child's Parent Pay account on a half termly basis. You will only pay for the sessions that your child attends.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Shared Purpose - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
We bring together an environment that is built on trust, collaboration and mutual support. This is essential in guaranteeing a workplace where your voice is heard and help is always available when needed.
As a team, we believe in overcoming challenges as a collective to ensure we keep our shared goals in focus. Especially, since we recognise that everyone may face different circumstances.
We know that by working as a unified team, we’ll be able to achieve great things and flourish into a positive, inclusive environment for all. Our approach has four key principles:
Belonging: Acceptance, Inclusion, Shared Values, Shared Purpose
Collegial relationships: Respect, Civility, Trust
Recognition & appreciation: Acknowledge, Celebrate, Empower
Psychological safety: Ask questions, Admit mistakes, Take risks
This approach helps staff see how their role fits into the bigger picture of our school, motivating them to want to make a difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Club - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
The Cyril Jackson After School Club launched in September 2016 and is for children from Reception to Year 6. It runs every day, in school term-time, straight after school until 5.30pm in the North Building. We offer a wide programme of after school clubs which change on a termly basis.
There are two sessions:
Session One is between 3.30pm to 4.30pm when a variety of exciting clubs take place, such as cooking, football, art, mixed sports, archery, sewing and more. The cost for is £5 per child or £4 each for siblings and those eligible for statutory free school meals.
Session Two is between 4.30pm - 5.30pm which offers parents and carers who may be studying or working with extra wrap-around provision where children can do homework, play games, read books, learn new skills and have a relaxing second hour. Snacks are drinks are provided for both sessions. The cost for is £5 per child or £4 each for siblings and those eligible for statutory free school meals.
All clubs are inclusive and available to all children. If a club is very popular, priority for places will be given to working parents.
Exciting clubs will be on offer each term and based on popular demand. Letters will go out each term for you to sign up.
If you require after school provision at any time please contact the school office for available spaces.
Fees will be added to your child’s Parent Pay account on a half termly basis. You will pay for those clubs that you sign your child up for. If your child is sick or absent then you will still need to pay for the sessions that you have signed your child up for.

pageCache.pageTitle: CPD – Development & Learning Opportunities - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our CPD curriculum
We believe that CPD (continuous professional development) for staff should reflect a similar structure as the curriculum for pupils. This is inspired by Zoe and Mark Enser’s The CPD Curriculum (2021).
Our staff training program is based on the school's priorities, it follows a curriculum-like design where CPD training is planned out for the entire academic year. This way the team will receive high-quality training with a clear outcome in mind.
The programme follows three key principles:
This strategy ensures our staff are always equipped to be their best, which aligns with the educational development of our students.
Intent: To achieve our schools priorities
Our CPD vision
We believe that everyone is entitled to professional development and growth. This is why we are committed to providing a high-quality tailored CPD programme that’ll ensure improvements across our staff body.
We facilitate bespoke CPD opportunities because personal development is the building block of our core values. Tapping into the diverse skill sets within our team, we celebrate everyone's best practices.
Our CPD training is strategically planned out including recommendations from the Education Endowment Foundation’s guidance report on Effective Professional Development. We focus on evidence-based training ensuring the entire staff body progresses within their skill set, not just in teaching and learning.
The individual CPD sessions follow Kolb’s Experiential Learning Cycle, where time is allocated to staff so they can put the theory and research into practice. Feedback is always welcome, as our staff are provided the time to share insights into how their learning experience can improve for the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Hodo - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Cyril Jackson and all the opportunities that await because we are known for inspiring and educating both our staff and students. We are proud to be a part of a Multi-Academy Trust like University Schools Trust, which collaborates with schools from across the London boroughs.
I was educated at St Paul’s Way School and, therefore a proud product of this borough. I know what the power of outstanding education can accomplish, it’s a privilege to be able to play a part in our student's futures.
The only way to achieve our dream of inspiring tomorrow’s leaders is by working as one unified team.
This is why having equity and strong social justice is at the heart of everything we do, whether that be within teaching or another role. By joining Cyril Jackson, you’ll be part of a dedicated community of professionals working together to uplift the lives of many children and families.
Our staff are geared up with all the essential tools they need to succeed. We host a tailored Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Programme, because we believe in aiding our staff to grow so they can take ownership of their roles, and truly flourish. This career development is central to a career at Cyril Jackson.
I encourage you to experience Cyril Jackson firsthand! I invite all possible candidates to visit the school for a tour. This is the best way to see the school in action, meet our team, and learn what makes Cyril Jackson special.
To ensure your experience here is impactful, we live by three key pledges:
I look forward to meeting you and welcoming you to the Cyril Jackson family.
Hodo Dirir Headteacher

As a school our top priority is to create a safe and nurturing environment for every child. Through our safeguarding policies and practices, we aim to protect our students from harm and ensure they have the confidence to learn, thrive, and grow. Every child's well-being and safety are at the heart of everything we do.
Cyril Jackson Primary School follows the procedures outlined by the Tower Hamlets Local Safeguarding Children Board - a guide to procedure and practice for all professional staff in Tower Hamlets who work with children.
Please direct any concerns or queries regarding safeguarding or child protection to the DSL, Hodo Dirir via safeguarding@cyriljackson.towerhamlets.sch.uk
Safeguarding Team
Meet our school safeguarding team, led by our designated safeguarding lead (DSL) who holds overall responsibility for safeguarding, supported by a team of deputy safeguarding leads (DDSL’s) to ensure our students and school community are safe and supported.
Hodo Dirir – Headteacher, DSL Maryum Qureshi - Deputy Headteacher, DDSL Joshua Chivers - Deputy Headteacher, DDSL Leonie Stafford-Williams – Assistant Headteacher, DDSL Anna Lindsay – Assistant Headteacher, DDSL Jesslyn Holman – Assistant Headteacher, DDSL Alysha Kassam – Assitant Headteacher, DDSL Alex Hunt – Inclusion and Safeguarding Lead and Executive Assistant, DDSL Shopna Rani – Inclusion, Data and Admissions Officer, DDSL Rukeya Begum – Home School Liason, DDSL Lipi Islam – Home School Liason, DDSL
More Safeguarding Information
Managing disclosures
If any student discloses that they are thinking of harming themselves, others or if someone is harming them, the safeguarding team must be notified immediately.
Confidentiality
If a child shares sensitive information, our staff are trained to handle it with utmost care, discretion and transparency. They will discuss confidentiality and its limits with the child.
If there's a concern about harm or safety, the child will be informed first if that confidentiality may need be broken, to make sure they get the right help and support.
In some cases, if there are deeper child protection concerns, you might not be directly informed, but our DSL Hodo Dirir and the school safeguarding team will be alerted through CPOMs.
Please know that whatever your child confides will only be shared with necessary staff to ensure their well-being. For a comprehensive understanding, please refer to our Safeguarding Policy.
Online Safety
We recognise the importance of online safety in today's digital age. We encourage parents to be proactive in ensuring their child's safety online. Taking steps to enable children to make the safe choices. This could include discussion around the content they watch, apps they use, time they spend on devices or if/who they are talking to others online. If you have any concerns or need guidance on online safety, please don't hesitate to contact the school. For more please see our Online Safety page.
Signposting
Domestic Abuse
The Home Office has created domestic abuse guidance in Bengali, Somali, English and other languages. The guidance explains how to recognise and report domestic abuse and where victims and perpetrators can access support. Please visit the website to find out how to get help if you or someone you know is a victim of domestic abuse.

pageCache.pageTitle: CJ Curriculum - Cyril Jackson Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Vision
At Cyril Jackson Primary School our exceptional curriculum is ambitious; we hold high expectations for all our pupils and learning is sequenced to ensure they leave our school fully prepared for the opportunities and challenges they may face in their future and in all that they aspire to do. We foster a ‘love of learning’ where pupils mature into enthusiastic, resilient learners.
Our broad and balanced curriculum is carefully planned to enable progression in key knowledge and subject specific skills from Early Years all the way through to Year 6. Content is sequenced to ensure that component knowledge leads to conceptual understanding; pupils are encouraged to make connections across year groups and subjects, therefore enabling them to think more deeply and interrogate subject matter. Key themes and enquiry questions are embedded throughout subjects to allow pupils to make meaningful links between current learning and that which came before. By spacing the content of our curriculum in this way, we provide pupils with regular opportunities to retrieve and recall prior learning and thus commit learning to their long-term memory.
At Cyril Jackson our curriculum goes far beyond the National Curriculum; we have thoughtfully designed units of work to ensure they are relevant to our pupils and are responsive to what is going on in the world. Our curriculum design is evidence based and informed by research to ensure all pupils are challenged. It is structured to empower pupils and enable them to make autonomous decisions that affect change. Pupils are motivated to understand the world around them; learning is rooted in a wider sense of citizenship and the environment. Curriculum design for us is a continuous dynamic process whereby assessment informs the design of our future learning. The curriculum is constantly evolving as it is adapted and personalised for pupils - it is crucial to us that our curriculum offer is equitable for all.
The Cyril Jackson curriculum encompasses academic learning from the classroom, but also incorporates our high expectations of them as respectful individuals and how they should become kind and curious people outside of school. Our school values are embedded in every subject to ensure all pupils leave Cyril Jackson as passionate individuals with high aspirations for themselves and those around them.
Curriculum Overviews
These documents show details of the topics you can expect your child to cover in each year at Cyril Jackson.
Curriculum Progression
The purpose of these documents is to support staff with having an expert knowledge of curriculum progression in every subject throughout a pupil's journey at Cyril Jackson Primary School.
Each subject-specific progression document enables the viewer to see 'what comes before and what comes next' in each area of learning and can be used as a benchmark to indicate the prior knowledge or pupils when commencing new topics or year groups. In addition, each document supports staff with assessing children's depth of knowledge at the end of each unit.
All subjects demonstrate our intent and elements of implementation.
